covers.quote: Use italics and sentence case for artwork titles

Sometimes the artist has made a different typographic choice for the title. If so, follow the capitalisation of the original. Include any numbers or punctuation in exactly the same way as the artist does.
From the second mention, you can use a shortened version of the name if it makes sense.
If the title is in another language, write it in that language. Use the exact spelling. You can include the English translation of the title.
Sometimes people call works of art by a name other than that given to them by the artist. Italicise the informal names of artworks in the same way that you would with the formal titles.
Sometimes an artist may choose to call a work ‘Untitled’or not give it a name. Write ‘Untitled’ in italics with an initial capital letter. Include the year of production and the artist’s name.
You might not be able to find the year of production. In this case, include the artist’s name and the medium of the work in square brackets.

examples.note: Sentence case and italics for artwork title and subsequent shortened mention.

parts.quote: Margaret Olley’s Portrait in the mirror is one of her notable works. Portrait is usually included in retrospectives of Olley’s work.

examples.note: Capitalisation following artist's original.

parts.quote: Parliament’s forecourt mosaic is based on Michael Nelson Jagamara’s Possum and Wallaby Dreaming.

examples.note: Informal name Blue poles italicised in sentence case.

parts.quote: Jackson Pollock titled his 1952 work Number 11 before it became known as Blue poles in a 1954 exhibition.

examples.note: Untitled italicised with capital U and year.

parts.quote: Hunter’s Untitled (1968) is part of the permanent collection in the Museum of Contemporary Art.

examples.note: Untitled italicised with medium in square brackets when year is unknown.

parts.quote: Dinh’s Untitled [oil on hardboard] was recently purchased for a private collection.

rules.quote: Italicise the titles of individual artworks and use sentence case.
rules.violation_condition: the title of an individual artwork is not written in italics or is not in sentence case (unless following the artist's original typography)
when: If the artist made a different typographic choice for the title, follow the capitalisation, numbers, or punctuation of the original.
From the second mention, a shortened version of the name can be used if it makes sense.
If the title is in another language, write it in that language using the exact spelling (English translation may be included).
Italicise informal names of artworks in the same way as formal titles.
For untitled works, write 'Untitled' in italics with an initial capital letter, including year of production and artist's name (or artist name and medium in square brackets if year is unknown).
rules.why: G-1, G-2, G-4: Rule heading and body combined with variations for original typography, foreign titles, informal titles, and untitled works.

covers.quote: Use title case and italics for artwork series
Modern works in a series might not use capital letters at all.

examples.note: Potter series in italics and title case.

parts.quote: The exhibition included Coffin with flowers and potter’s wheel with landscape decoration, a drawing in the Potter series by Arthur Boyd.

examples.note: Flight Research series in italics and title case, while modern work title respects artist styling.

parts.quote: flight research #6 is part of Rosemary Laing’s Flight Research series.

rules.quote: Write the titles of series of unique works of art in italics. Use title case (maximal capitalisation). Write the titles of the individual works of art in the series in italics, too. Capitalise and punctuate according to the original title.
rules.violation_condition: the title of an artwork series is not italicised or not written in title case (unless the modern original uses no capitals)
when: Modern works in a series might not use capital letters at all.
rules.why: G-2, G-4: Merges heading and body instruction with modern styling exception.

covers.quote: Use roman type for exhibition titles

examples.note: Exhibition title 'Water' in roman type.

parts.quote: Cai Guo-Qiang’s Heritage(2013) is part of GOMA’s Water exhibition.

examples.note: Exhibition title in roman type.

parts.quote: The Asia Pacific Triennial attracts visitors from all over Australia.

rules.quote: Write the titles of exhibitions in roman type and use the same capitalisation as the museum or gallery uses.
rules.violation_condition: the title of an exhibition is written in italics rather than roman type, or does not follow the gallery's capitalisation
rules.why: G-4: Heading restated in body sentence.

covers.quote: Use italics for titles of exhibition catalogues

examples.note: Catalogue title in italics and sentence case.

parts.quote: The Philip Bacon Galleries produced a catalogue named Important Australian paintings.It accompanied the 2011 exhibition of the same name.

rules.quote: Treat catalogues as books. Write catalogue titles in italics and use sentence case for the title.
rules.violation_condition: the title of an exhibition catalogue is not written in italics or is not in sentence case
rules.why: G-4: Heading restated by body sentence with sentence case requirement.

covers.quote: Include the name of the exhibition and the format of the catalogue in the reference list. After the title of the exhibition, include the full start and end dates for the exhibition.

For online catalogues, hyperlink the title of the catalogue and include an accessed date. If the catalogue is a PDF, link to the page where the PDF is hosted, instead of to the PDF. If you can’t link to a host page, include ‘PDF’ in square brackets after the format information.
Rule: Author or Gallery Name (Year) Title of exhibition [format] [PDF], Day Month Year of exhibition, Publisher, Place, accessed Day Month Year.

examples.note: Print exhibition catalogue reference list entry.

parts.quote: Philip Bacon Gallery (2011) Important Australian paintings [printed exhibition catalogue], 31 May to 25 June 2011, Philip Bacon Galleries, Brisbane.

examples.note: Online exhibition catalogue reference list entry.

parts.quote: Campbell H (2010) Colour, rhythm, design: wood & lino cuts of the 20s and 30s [online exhibition catalogue], 13 March to 11 July 2010, Art Gallery of NSW, Sydney, accessed 23 February 2020.

rules.quote: Rule: Author or Gallery Name (Year) Title of exhibition [format], Day Month Year of exhibition, Publisher, Location of Gallery.
rules.violation_condition: an exhibition catalogue reference list entry does not follow the template 'Author or Gallery Name (Year) Title of exhibition [format], Day Month Year of exhibition, Publisher, Location of Gallery.' (or for online catalogues, does not include hyperlinked title, accessed date, and PDF bracket where required)
when: For online catalogues, hyperlink the title of the catalogue and include an accessed date.
If the online catalogue is a PDF, link to the page where the PDF is hosted instead of to the PDF; if impossible, include '[PDF]' after the format information.
rules.why: G-2: Consolidates print and online exhibition catalogue reference formatting rules.

covers.quote: Rule: Creator Full Name (Year) Title or description of work [medium], Website, Exhibition or Gallery, Location of Gallery, © Creator, courtesy: Creator or Gallery, accessed Date Month Year.

examples.note: Digital image caption.

parts.quote: Megan Cope (1982) Quandamooka people[hand-cast concrete oyster shells, copper slag, foam support structure], RE FORMATION 2019, Australia, © and image courtesy: Megan Cope.

rules.quote:
If your content features an image of an artwork, it must accompanied by a caption with:

the full details of the work of art

copyright and permission information, if necessary.
rules.violation_condition: an image of an artwork in digital content lacks a caption providing the full details of the work and copyright/permission information
rules.why: G-1, G-2: Specific rule for captions accompanying artwork images in digital content.

covers.quote: Write long captions in this order:
Write short captions in this order:

examples.note: Short caption style.

parts.quote: Snake (Rainbow Serpent)
wall painting
Museum of Old and New Art, Hobart

rules.quote: For each collection, exhibition or catalogue, use either a long or short caption style and use that style consistently. If it’s a solo exhibition, don’t include the artist’s name on each artwork.
rules.violation_condition: captions in a collection, exhibition, or catalogue mix short and long styles inconsistently, or include the artist's name on each artwork in a solo exhibition, or do not follow the designated field order
when: If it is a solo exhibition, do not include the artist's name on each artwork.
Long caption order: artist, title of artwork, year of creation, medium, size, name of museum/gallery, date of acquisition, location of museum/gallery, whether the work is part of a bequest.
Short caption order: artist, year of creation, title of artwork, medium, name of museum/gallery, location of museum/gallery.
rules.why: G-2: Consolidates caption style consistency and long/short element orders into one captioning rule.

covers.quote: Mention the name of the museum or gallery in text

examples.note: Mentions holding institution MONA.

parts.quote: The Sydney Nolan Gallery in MONA houses Snake, a 46-metre artwork by Sydney Nolan.

rules.quote: When you write about artwork, include the name of the institution that holds the work in its collection.
rules.specification: When an artwork held in an institutional collection is discussed in text, name the gallery or museum.
rules.violation_condition: prose discussing an artwork does not mention the name of the holding institution

examples.note: In-text citation with author, title, and year.

parts.quote: The collection includes Long (The spirit of the plains 1897). [In-text citation]

rules.quote: For in-text citations, include the artist, year of creation and title of the artwork in parentheses. Depending on the type of publication, you might include other details (such as the medium or format).
rules.violation_condition: an in-text citation for an artwork lacks artist, year of creation, or title in parentheses
rules.why: G-2: In-text citation requirement for artworks.

covers.quote: List artworks after the main reference list
Rule: Creator C (Year) Title or description of work [medium], Website, Exhibition or Gallery, Location of Gallery, accessed Date Month Year.

examples.note: Artwork reference list entry placed after main reference list.

parts.quote: Long S (1897) The spirit of the plains[painting], Queensland Art Gallery, Brisbane, Australia. [Reference list entry]

rules.quote: Include the full source information in a list of artworks after the reference list.
rules.violation_condition: artwork reference entries are placed in the main reference list rather than a separate list of artworks after the reference list, or do not follow 'Creator C (Year) Title or description of work [medium], Website, Exhibition or Gallery, Location of Gallery, accessed Date Month Year.'
rules.why: G-1, G-4: Merges heading, body instruction, and reference list format template.
